posts.name: LewdDolphin21
posts.cooked:
I played Imbued Fire immediately, making sure I never dealt Absolute Zero cold damage unintentionally, but I had no need to deal him cold damage anyway. I played Grease Gun after a Primeval Eruption, but then realized Akash'bhuta couldn't deal herself damage with that out, so I just stalled a round instead of killing everything like I had originally planned. I played Subzero Atmosphere smartly, making sure not to destroy it during Akash'bhuta's play phase, and actually spared the team a lot of damage from Living Rockslides (actually, no Rockslide ever dealt damage, which was cool). The last round featured a lot of shenanigans, between K.N.Y.F.E.'s Incidental Contact comboing with Flawless Execution, Incidental Contact and Imbued Fire having Absolute Zero do damage twice on K.N.Y.F.E.'s turn, Hoarfire doing a lot of damage because of Absolute Zero hitting himself for fire three times, and finishing with Ra's Inferno also hitting Absolute Zero in addition to Akash'bhuta and all Primeval Limbs. She had started that round at 95 HP.

The only unfortunate thing was that Tempest could not deal damage after the second round, due to the annoying Brambles (though he was partially responsible for it, having thrown one into the stratosphere...).

posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Fine.

 

Boy, I had a series of very close games that didn't quite make it.  In the second game, with only Mr. Fixer and KNYFE left (Fixer at 2HP, and KNYFE at 1HP) I thought I had it perfectly set up for the win. Char would be brought back by Tempest's incap power to clear the board of dmaged limbs and wipe out Akash'Bhuta. Turns out, I forgot to factor in that because Ra had recently been incapped, Imbued Fire was no longer in play. This did clear the board of limbs, but becasue of my brainfart, Akash'bhuta was left with 1HP. Then Char burned the heroes to a crisp. Ugh.

 

Watched LewdDolphin's video--the main difference between my play and his was that he had Tempest play Localized Hurricane to draw a bunch, which led to an Into the Stratosphere that I never saw in my games. That proves to be a BIG factor -- by gumming up the villain deck and making that Prison Riot/Primeval Eruption combo less scary (still scary, but less so).

 

Anyway, I finally beat it.

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
Mint. This was easier than I expected, given the setup.  I just kept knocking everything out round-by-round until her megaturn.  The most critical decisions I had to make were these:

- At one point, I had to choose whether Tempest or F6AZ would take a hit, making them the lowest HP, making them the target of the Brambles. I chose Tempest; despite the fact that he had two Lightning Slashes in hand, I figured keeping AZ around with Cold Snap + Imbued Fire would be worth more through the course of the game.  Plus, Tempest could actually do stuff without dealing damage (Aquatic Correspondence, Subwave Inducer, Ball Lightning).

- I had 7 Ongoings out when AB decided she was destroying 5 Ongoings.  I kept Cold Snap and Impale out, destroying everything else (Imbued Fire, Battlefield Experience, Flawless Execution, Grievous Hailstorm, and Living Conflagration.)  Basically, I had another copy of three of those in hand already, and blowing up BE made me draw another one anyway, so no big loss.

Akash'Bhuta's mega-turn ended up being painful, but I still had Grease Gun, so I threw that out and used the round off to chip away at Mountainous Carapaces and recover my Ongoings (and Isothermic Transducer) that got destroyed.  Once Imbued Fire was back out, I went berserk in the final round and took down her entire board, including a glorious Imbued Fire-boosted Incidental Contact that caused AZ to deal out an additional 6 damage.  We finished the job on Ra's power usage before she could start going through her freshly reshuffled deck.

Mr. Fixer (12 HP) - Could have been a lot more useful, actually, but having so many copies of Charge and Overdrive was enough.  Never played any equipment (only saw Tire Iron), only got to play Grease Monkey Fist right at the end.

KNYFE (10 HP) - Punch stuff with base power, used Energy Burn ASAP when it came up, threw out a couple Ongoings that didn't help much.  Incidental Contact was her finest moment.

PW Tempest (7 HP) - Lots of Hailstorm until it got blown up, used Ball Lightning to knock out an Entomb despite being unable to do damage.  Never used his base power.  Somehow never got around to using Lightning Slash, which felt weird. I did use a Chain Lightning though.

F6 Absolute Zero (5 HP) - Pulled Transducers with each Onboard Module Installation I got. Cold Snap first, then Impale, then just kept chipping away at things with his base power. Used Fueled Freeze as soon as I got it, destroyed one of KNYFE's ongoings to make it 2 damage (in addition to destroying the Allies of the Earth). Only hit him with fire twice (Incidental Contact). Guess I could have done it again, but I didn't know I'd have the HP to spare. I got Subzero Atmosphere one turn too late for it to have done any good.

Ra (9 HP) - Imbued Fire, Staff, start burning things.  I threw out Conflagration as a one-shot but never used the power. Good thing, too, as I only got A'B dead by a margin of 2 HP on Ra's last turn, and who knows what that next turn would have been.  Anyway, he finally got to throw out Inferno on the last turn. 

-

I tried it again by annihilating F6AZ as fast as possible (round 2) and stunlocking the environment - the final HP values then were 17, 15, 13, 0, 21. Probably could have done a little better than that, it made the battle utterly trivial. A'B didn't even survive to play a Rockslide.

posts.name: deddragon
posts.cooked:
Got a Near Mint after a few critical early mistakes in the first game.

Absolute Zero was a big damage dealer in my winning game, couldn’t have done it without him. I got Thermal Shockwave out, which combined with Isothermic Transducer and Imbued Fire was doing 2 damage 4 times each round with only 1 damage to himself.
KNYFE didn’t have her own buffs, so she took advantage of the fire as well. Do I want to hit AZ a second time with Incidental Contact? Yes, yes I do.
Like has been said, Excavation was really handy to help keep Akash from flipping and giving a little respite from limbs. And of course Ra bounced a little Inferno damage off Zero when he ran out of targets.
Tempest spent a few turns unable to do damage, but still contributed with a Ball Lightning and some Correspondence on those rounds. Did some damage on other rounds with a burning Hurricane.
Not Fixer’s best match but he did 2-5 damage most rounds.
I enjoyed arranging for Guards to hit limbs when they were out. I even let Char get the killing blow on Akash.
Everyone was up at the end, though Tempest was at 1 and Absolute Zero was at 2.
